description: Running `alembic upgrade head` on an empty SQLite file creates tables users, patient_profiles, patient_profile_versions, doctor_profiles, availability_templates, slots, appointments, appointment_events and consultation_notes.
steps: Run alembic upgrade head against a fresh database file
Query sqlite_master for table names
Assert all nine table names are present

description: UPDATE and DELETE statements against patient_profile_versions, appointment_events and consultation_notes are each rejected by a SQLite trigger and leave the row unchanged.
steps: Insert one row into each of the three tables
Execute UPDATE on each and assert an IntegrityError/abort is raised
Execute DELETE on each and assert the same
Re-read rows and assert they are unchanged

description: A fee of Decimal('500.00') is persisted as the integer 50000, read back as Decimal('500.00'), and no float type appears in fee or money code paths.
steps: Save a doctor profile with fee Decimal('500.00') via the repository
Run raw SQL and assert the column value is the integer 50000
Read via the repository and assert Decimal('500.00')
Grep money modules and assert no float annotations or float() calls

description: Every new SQLite connection reports journal_mode 'wal' and a busy_timeout of at least 5000 ms.
steps: Open a connection through the engine factory
Execute PRAGMA journal_mode and assert 'wal'
Execute PRAGMA busy_timeout and assert >= 5000

description: Inserting a slot with a status outside AVAILABLE/BOOKED/BLOCKED, or an appointment with a status outside BOOKED/CHECKED_IN/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/CANCELLED/NO_SHOW, is rejected by a CHECK constraint.
steps: Insert a slot with status 'FOO' and assert IntegrityError
Insert an appointment with status 'FOO' and assert IntegrityError
Insert valid values and assert success

description: GET /health returns 200 with body {"status":"ok"} within 1 second of the process starting.
steps: Start the backend with `npm start` or uvicorn and record the start time
Poll GET /health until the first response
Assert status 200, body status 'ok' and elapsed time < 1s from listening

description: Every response carries an X-Request-ID header: a valid incoming value is echoed back, and a missing or invalid value is replaced by a generated UUID.
steps: GET /health with X-Request-ID 'abc-123' and assert the same value in the response header
GET /health with no header and assert a UUID-format value
GET /health with an over-long or illegal-character value and assert a generated UUID

description: Each log line is valid JSON containing correlation_id, and a request whose body contains an email, name or note text produces log lines that contain none of those values.
steps: Capture logs while POSTing a body containing a unique email and name
Parse every log line as JSON and assert correlation_id exists
Assert the unique email and name strings appear in no log line

description: SlotUnavailableException and InvalidAppointmentStateException map to 409, naive datetimes and malformed input map to 422, and a SQLite lock timeout maps to 503 with a generic body.
steps: Raise each exception from a test route and assert 409
Send a naive datetime and assert 422
Simulate OperationalError 'database is locked' and assert 503
Assert the 503 body contains no SQL or stack trace text

description: Settings load PROVIDER_TIMEZONE (default UTC), JWT lifetime, database path and busy timeout from environment, and an unknown timezone name aborts startup with an error naming PROVIDER_TIMEZONE.
steps: Start with no env and assert provider timezone is UTC
Start with PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata and assert it is applied
Start with PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=Mars/Base and assert a non-zero exit with the variable name in the message

description: POST /api/auth/register with a valid email, an 8+ character password and a valid profile (full_name, age, gender, phone) returns 201 with a non-null user_id and role PATIENT.
steps: POST /api/auth/register with email 'p1@example.test', password 'correct-horse', full_name 'Test Patient', age 34, gender 'FEMALE' and phone '+91-555-0100'
Assert status 201
Assert body contains non-null user_id and role 'PATIENT'
Assert the response body contains no password or hash

description: A role field supplied in the registration body is ignored and the created user always has role PATIENT.
steps: Use a valid profile (full_name, age, gender, phone) in every registration request
POST /api/auth/register with body including "role":"ADMIN"
Assert status 201
Read the user from the database and assert role is PATIENT

description: Registering an email that already exists, compared case-insensitively, returns 409.
steps: Use a valid profile (full_name, age, gender, phone) in every registration request
Register 'dup@example.test'
Register 'DUP@example.test'
Assert second response status 409
Assert only one user row exists

description: Passwords of 7 characters or 129 characters return 422, while passwords of exactly 8 and exactly 128 characters are accepted.
steps: Use a valid profile (full_name, age, gender, phone) in every registration request
Register with a 7-char password and assert 422
Register with a 129-char password and assert 422
Register with an 8-char password and assert 201
Register with a 128-char password and assert 201

description: The stored password_hash starts with '$argon2' and never equals the plaintext password.
steps: Use a valid profile (full_name, age, gender, phone) in every registration request
Register a user with password 'correct-horse'
Read password_hash from the database
Assert it starts with '$argon2' and differs from the plaintext

description: POST /api/auth/login with correct credentials returns 200 and a JWT access token with an expiry; a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated account all return 401 with the identical generic body.
steps: Login with correct credentials and assert 200 and a decodable token with an exp claim
Login with a wrong password, an unknown email and a deactivated account
Assert all three return 401 with byte-identical JSON bodies

description: A request to a protected route with no token, a malformed token or an expired token returns 401.
steps: Call a protected route with no Authorization header and assert 401
Call with 'Bearer garbage' and assert 401
Call with a token whose exp is in the past and assert 401

description: The role is read from the database, so a valid token claiming role ADMIN for a user whose stored role is PATIENT receives 403 on an admin route.
steps: Create a patient and forge a validly signed token with role claim ADMIN
Call an /api/admin route
Assert 403

description: A user with the wrong role for a route receives 403, and a user of the right role requesting another user's object receives 404.
steps: Call a doctor-only route as a patient and assert 403
Call GET /api/appointments/{id} as patient B for patient A's appointment and assert 404

description: A user deactivated after logging in has the still-valid token rejected with 401 on the next request.
steps: Login as a patient and keep the token
Deactivate the user directly in the database
Call a protected route with the token and assert 401

description: An ADMIN user receives 200 on patient routes, doctor routes and admin routes when the object exists.
steps: Login as admin
Call a patient-scoped GET, a doctor-scoped GET and an admin GET
Assert each returns 200

description: GET /api/patients/me/profile returns 200 with the latest profile version for the logged-in patient.
steps: Register and login as a patient
GET /api/patients/me/profile
Assert 200 and full_name, age, gender and phone match the registration data

description: PUT /api/patients/me/profile inserts a new version row and leaves all earlier version rows byte-identical.
steps: PUT a changed phone number (other profile fields omitted and carried forward)
Count patient_profile_versions rows and assert it increased by exactly 1
Compare earlier rows with a snapshot taken before and assert they are unchanged

description: After two successive updates, GET /api/patients/me/profile returns the values from the second update.
steps: PUT value A then PUT value B
GET the profile
Assert it returns value B

description: A doctor calling /api/patients/me/profile receives 403 and a patient requesting another patient's profile by id receives 404.
steps: Login as a doctor and call GET /api/patients/me/profile, assert 403
Login as patient B and GET /api/patients/{A-id}/profile, assert 404

description: A profile update writes a log line containing user_id but none of the submitted profile values.
steps: Capture logs while PUT-ing a unique name and phone
Assert a line includes user_id
Assert the unique name and phone appear in no log line

description: A template of Monday 09:00-12:00 with 30-minute slots yields exactly 6 AVAILABLE slots for each Monday in the next 14 days.
steps: Freeze the clock to a known Sunday
Run the generator for a doctor with a Monday 09:00-12:00/30 template
Assert exactly 6 slots per Monday in range, all with status AVAILABLE and 30-minute duration

description: Slots are created only when now < start < now + 14 days; a slot starting in the past or 14 days or more ahead is never created.
steps: Freeze the clock mid-way through a template day
Run the generator
Assert no slot has start <= now
Assert no slot has start >= now + 14 days

description: Running the generator twice produces the same slot count and no duplicate (doctor_id, start) rows.
steps: Run the generator and record the slot count
Run it again
Assert the count is unchanged and a GROUP BY doctor_id,start HAVING count>1 query returns zero rows

description: With PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata, a 09:00 template time is stored as 03:30 UTC.
steps: Set PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata
Generate slots for a 09:00 template
Assert the stored start time is 03:30 UTC

description: Starting the app after the clock advanced 5 days creates the slots for the newly in-window days without duplicating existing ones.
steps: Generate slots at day 0
Advance the clock 5 days and run application startup
Assert new slots exist for days 14-19 and no duplicate rows exist

description: POST /api/admin/doctors with valid details returns 201 with a doctor_id, creates a user with role DOCTOR, stores the fee as "500.00", and generates slots for the next 14 days.
steps: Login as admin
POST /api/admin/doctors with specialty, languages ['en','hi'], fee '500.00', initial password and a Monday 09:00-12:00/30 template
Assert 201 and non-null doctor_id
Assert the user has role DOCTOR
Assert 6 slots exist per Monday in range

description: A non-admin caller receives 403 and an unauthenticated caller receives 401 on POST /api/admin/doctors.
steps: POST as patient and assert 403
POST as doctor and assert 403
POST with no token and assert 401

description: A template whose end is not after start, whose slot length is zero or negative, or whose slot length does not divide the window returns 422 and persists nothing.
steps: POST with end == start and assert 422
POST with slot length 0 and assert 422
POST with a 100-minute window and 30-minute slots and assert 422
Assert user, profile, template and slot counts are unchanged

description: A fee that is non-numeric, negative or has more than 2 decimal places returns 422.
steps: POST with fee 'abc' and assert 422
POST with fee '-1.00' and assert 422
POST with fee '500.123' and assert 422

description: Onboarding with an email that already exists returns 409 and creates nothing.
steps: Onboard a doctor
Onboard again with the same email
Assert 409
Assert only one user row for the email

description: The newly onboarded doctor can log in with the admin-supplied initial password and receives a token whose database role is DOCTOR.
steps: Onboard a doctor with initial password
POST /api/auth/login with those credentials
Assert 200
Call a doctor-only route and assert 200

description: GET /api/doctors/me/slots?from=&to= returns only the caller's slots in the range with their status.
steps: Login as doctor A with doctor B also having slots
GET /api/doctors/me/slots for the next 7 days
Assert every returned slot belongs to doctor A and each has a status field

description: PUT /api/doctors/me/slots/{id}/block on an AVAILABLE slot returns 200 and the slot becomes BLOCKED.
steps: Pick an AVAILABLE slot
PUT block
Assert 200
Read the slot and assert BLOCKED

description: Blocking a BOOKED slot returns 409 and the slot and its appointment remain unchanged.
steps: Book a slot as a patient
PUT block as the doctor
Assert 409
Assert the slot is still BOOKED and the appointment still BOOKED

description: PUT /api/doctors/me/slots/{id}/unblock on a BLOCKED slot returns 200 and the slot becomes AVAILABLE, while unblocking a non-BLOCKED slot returns 409.
steps: Block a slot then PUT unblock and assert 200 and AVAILABLE
PUT unblock on an AVAILABLE slot and assert 409

description: A doctor blocking another doctor's slot receives 404 and a patient calling the block route receives 403.
steps: Login as doctor A and PUT block on doctor B's slot id, assert 404
Login as patient and PUT block, assert 403

description: GET /api/doctors?specialty=Cardiology returns only doctors with that specialty, and ?language=hi returns only doctors who speak that language.
steps: Seed doctors with different specialties and languages
GET with specialty filter and assert every result matches
GET with language filter and assert every result matches

description: GET /api/doctors?available_from=&available_to= returns only doctors with at least one AVAILABLE slot inside the range.
steps: Block or book all of doctor A's slots on day 3
GET with a day-3 range
Assert doctor A is absent and a doctor with open day-3 slots is present

description: The sort parameter orders results ascending by earliest open slot, by fee, or by name.
steps: GET ?sort=earliest_slot and assert nondecreasing earliest slot
GET ?sort=fee and assert nondecreasing fee
GET ?sort=name and assert alphabetical order

description: Each result includes the fee as a string such as "500.00" and the earliest open slot, and deactivated doctors never appear.
steps: Deactivate a doctor
GET /api/doctors
Assert the deactivated doctor is absent
Assert each result has fee matching ^\d+\.\d{2}$ and an earliest_slot field

description: GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots lists only AVAILABLE slots starting after now and within 14 days; BOOKED, BLOCKED and past slots are never listed.
steps: Set up AVAILABLE, BOOKED, BLOCKED and past slots for one doctor
GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots
Assert only the AVAILABLE future slots are returned

description: Unauthenticated calls to the search and slot endpoints return 401.
steps: GET /api/doctors with no token and assert 401
GET /api/doctors/{id}/slots with no token and assert 401

description: VideoService, PaymentService (charge and refund), PrescriptionService and NotificationService interfaces exist and the default application wiring binds a stub for each.
steps: Build the app with default settings
Resolve each interface from the dependency container
Assert each resolves to a stub implementation

description: Each stub call emits exactly one JSON log line containing only identifiers such as appointment_id and event type.
steps: Call each stub once with an appointment id
Capture logs and assert exactly one line per call
Assert each line contains appointment_id and no names, emails or free text

description: Stub calls leave the appointment_events row count unchanged.
steps: Count appointment_events rows
Call every stub method
Assert the row count is unchanged

description: The video stub returns a deterministic placeholder join URL containing the appointment id.
steps: Call VideoService.join_url for appointment 42 twice
Assert both calls return the same URL
Assert the URL contains '42'

description: A test can override any stub with a spy through dependency injection and read its recorded calls.
steps: Override PaymentService with a spy
Invoke a service that refunds
Assert the spy recorded exactly one refund call with the appointment id

description: POST /api/appointments with an AVAILABLE slot_id returns 201 with an appointment_id and status BOOKED, the slot becomes BOOKED, and exactly one BOOKED event is appended.
steps: Login as a patient
POST /api/appointments {slot_id}
Assert 201, non-null appointment_id and status BOOKED
Assert the slot is BOOKED
Assert exactly one appointment_events row of type BOOKED

description: 20 concurrent POST /api/appointments requests for the same slot return exactly one 201 and nineteen 409 responses, and none return 503.
steps: Create one AVAILABLE slot and 20 patient tokens
Fire 20 simultaneous POSTs for that slot
Assert exactly one 201
Assert exactly nineteen 409
Assert zero 503
Assert exactly one appointment row exists

description: Booking a BOOKED, BLOCKED, past or more-than-14-days-ahead slot returns 409 and creates no appointment.
steps: Attempt to book each of the four slot types
Assert 409 for each
Assert appointment count is unchanged

description: Booking a slot belonging to a deactivated doctor returns 409 even when the slot id is supplied directly.
steps: Deactivate a doctor
POST /api/appointments with one of that doctor's slot ids
Assert 409
Assert the slot is still AVAILABLE

description: Only PATIENT users may book: a doctor receives 403 and an unauthenticated caller receives 401.
steps: POST as doctor and assert 403
POST with no token and assert 401

description: A successful booking calls the payment stub exactly once and the response includes the fee as a string such as "500.00".
steps: Override PaymentService with a spy
Book a slot
Assert the spy charge call count is 1
Assert the response fee equals the doctor's fee string

description: A patient cancelling exactly 60:00 before start receives 200, the appointment becomes CANCELLED, the slot returns to AVAILABLE, one CANCELLED event is appended and the refund stub is called exactly once.
steps: Book a slot starting at now+60:00
Patient POST /api/appointments/{id}/cancel
Assert 200 and status CANCELLED
Assert slot AVAILABLE
Assert one CANCELLED event
Assert refund spy call count is 1

description: A patient cancelling at 59:59 before start, or after the start time, receives 409 and nothing changes and the refund stub is not called.
steps: Book a slot starting at now+59:59
Patient cancel and assert 409
Advance the clock past start and cancel again, assert 409
Assert appointment still BOOKED, no new events, refund spy count 0

description: A patient cancelling another patient's appointment receives 404.
steps: Patient A books
Patient B POST cancel on A's appointment
Assert 404
Assert A's appointment is still BOOKED

description: A doctor cancelling a BOOKED appointment 10 minutes before start receives 200, the slot becomes BLOCKED, the event records actor role DOCTOR and the refund stub is called exactly once.
steps: Book a slot starting at now+10 min
Doctor POST cancel
Assert 200 and CANCELLED
Assert slot BLOCKED
Assert the event actor_role is DOCTOR
Assert refund spy count is 1

description: Cancelling a CHECKED_IN, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW appointment returns 409 InvalidAppointmentStateException and appends no event.
steps: Move an appointment to each non-BOOKED state
POST cancel for each
Assert 409
Assert event count unchanged

description: POST /api/appointments/{id}/reschedule {new_slot_id} returns 200 with the same appointment_id, the new slot becomes BOOKED and the old slot becomes AVAILABLE.
steps: Book slot X
POST reschedule to open slot Y of the same doctor
Assert 200 and unchanged appointment_id
Assert slot Y BOOKED
Assert slot X AVAILABLE

description: A RESCHEDULED event is appended containing both the old slot id and the new slot id.
steps: Reschedule X to Y
Read the newest appointment_events row
Assert type RESCHEDULED, old_slot_id X and new_slot_id Y

description: A target slot that is booked, blocked, already started, outside the 14-day window, the same slot, or another doctor's returns 409 and changes nothing.
steps: Attempt reschedule to each of the six invalid targets
Assert 409 for each
Assert the appointment slot, both slots' statuses and event count are unchanged

description: Rescheduling less than 60 minutes before the current start returns 409, while exactly 60:00 before start returns 200.
steps: Book a slot at now+59:59 and reschedule, assert 409
Book a slot at now+60:00 and reschedule, assert 200

description: Rescheduling an appointment in CHECKED_IN, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW returns 409.
steps: Move an appointment to each non-BOOKED state
POST reschedule for each
Assert 409

description: If a failure is injected after the target slot is claimed, the transaction rolls back and both slots and the appointment keep their original state.
steps: Inject a failing event-insert via a test hook
POST reschedule
Assert a non-2xx response
Assert target slot AVAILABLE, old slot BOOKED, appointment slot unchanged

description: The doctor can move an appointment BOOKED to CHECKED_IN to IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED, each call returns 200, and exactly one event with actor role DOCTOR is appended per transition.
steps: POST /api/appointments/{id}/status {status:'CHECKED_IN'} then 'IN_PROGRESS' then 'COMPLETED'
Assert 200 each time
Assert the event count increased by exactly 1 per call
Assert actor_role is DOCTOR

description: Invalid transitions (BOOKED to IN_PROGRESS, BOOKED to COMPLETED, CHECKED_IN to CANCELLED, and any change from COMPLETED, CANCELLED or NO_SHOW) return 409 InvalidAppointmentStateException and append no event.
steps: Attempt each invalid transition
Assert 409 for each
Assert event count unchanged and status unchanged

description: NO_SHOW is refused with 409 before the start time and accepted with 200 from BOOKED or CHECKED_IN after the start time, and the slot stays BOOKED.
steps: Mark NO_SHOW before start and assert 409
Advance the clock past start and mark NO_SHOW from BOOKED, assert 200
Repeat from CHECKED_IN, assert 200
Assert slot status BOOKED

description: GET /api/doctors/me/queue?date=YYYY-MM-DD returns only the caller's appointments whose start falls on that date in PROVIDER_TIMEZONE, ordered by start time.
steps: Set PROVIDER_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata and create appointments at 23:30 and 00:30 local time on adjacent days
GET queue for the first date
Assert only the 23:30 appointment is present
Assert results are ordered ascending by start
Assert another doctor's appointments are absent

description: Each appointment response includes allowed_actions that match the state machine, and NO_SHOW appears only once the start time has passed.
steps: GET a BOOKED appointment before start and assert allowed_actions contains CHECKED_IN and not NO_SHOW
Advance the clock past start and assert NO_SHOW is present
GET a COMPLETED appointment and assert allowed_actions is empty

description: Only the appointment's doctor can transition it: another doctor receives 404 and a patient receives 403.
steps: Doctor B POST status on doctor A's appointment and assert 404
Patient POST status and assert 403

description: The appointment's doctor can POST /api/appointments/{id}/notes {text} after COMPLETED, receives 201 each time, and multiple notes accumulate.
steps: Complete an appointment
POST two notes as the doctor
Assert 201 twice
GET notes and assert both are present in creation order

description: Adding a note to an appointment that is not COMPLETED returns 409; another doctor receives 404 and a patient receives 403.
steps: POST a note while BOOKED and assert 409
POST as doctor B on a completed appointment of doctor A and assert 404
POST as the patient and assert 403

description: A note of 5000 characters is accepted, while 5001 characters or empty text returns 422.
steps: POST 5000-char text and assert 201
POST 5001-char text and assert 422
POST empty text and assert 422

description: PUT, PATCH and DELETE on a note return 405, and a direct SQL UPDATE or DELETE on consultation_notes is rejected by the trigger.
steps: Send PUT, PATCH and DELETE to /api/appointments/{id}/notes/{note_id} and assert 405
Run raw UPDATE and DELETE on consultation_notes and assert both raise errors

description: GET notes returns 200 to that appointment's patient, its doctor and an admin, and 404 to a different patient or a different doctor.
steps: GET as the patient, doctor and admin and assert 200
GET as another patient and assert 404
GET as another doctor and assert 404

description: Posting a note logs the appointment_id and user_id but never the note text.
steps: Capture logs while POSTing a note with a unique marker string
Assert a line contains the appointment_id
Assert the marker string appears in no log line

description: GET /api/admin/users returns all users with role and active flag, and ?role=DOCTOR filters to doctors only.
steps: Seed one admin, two doctors and two patients
GET /api/admin/users and assert 5 rows with role and active fields
GET ?role=DOCTOR and assert 2 rows

description: Deactivating a patient returns 200, after which that patient's login returns 401, their existing token returns 401, and their existing appointments remain and can still be processed by the doctor.
steps: Book an appointment as patient P
Admin PUT /api/admin/users/{P}/deactivate and assert 200
Patient login and old token both return 401
Doctor checks the appointment in and assert 200

description: Deactivating a doctor with a BOOKED, CHECKED_IN or IN_PROGRESS appointment returns 409, while a doctor with only terminal appointments deactivates with 200 and disappears from search.
steps: Deactivate a doctor with a BOOKED appointment and assert 409
Complete the appointment and deactivate again, assert 200
GET /api/doctors and assert the doctor is absent

description: An admin deactivating their own account receives 409 and remains active.
steps: Admin PUT deactivate on own id
Assert 409
Read the user and assert active is true

description: Reactivating a user returns 200, the user can log in again, and a reactivated doctor reappears in search.
steps: Deactivate then PUT reactivate a doctor
Doctor login returns 200
GET /api/doctors and assert the doctor is present

description: PUT /api/admin/patients/{patient_id}/profile with changed full_name, age, gender or phone inserts a new profile version for that patient and leaves earlier versions unchanged.
steps: Admin PUT changed profile fields for patient P
Assert 200
Assert version count increased by 1
Assert earlier rows unchanged

description: GET /api/appointments/mine returns only the caller's appointments ordered by start time, each with status, fee string, doctor name and allowed_actions.
steps: Patients A and B each book appointments
GET mine as A
Assert only A's appointments, ordered by start
Assert each has status, fee, doctor name and allowed_actions

description: GET /api/appointments/{id} for another patient's appointment returns 404, for the appointment's own doctor or an admin returns 200.
steps: GET as patient B for A's appointment and assert 404
GET as A's doctor and assert 200
GET as admin and assert 200

description: For a patient, allowed_actions includes CANCEL and RESCHEDULE when start minus now is at least 60 minutes and excludes both inside that window.
steps: Book a slot at now+60:00 and assert both actions present
Advance the clock by 1 second and assert both absent

description: join_url is non-null for the patient and the doctor while the status is BOOKED, CHECKED_IN or IN_PROGRESS, and null for COMPLETED, CANCELLED and NO_SHOW.
steps: GET an appointment in each of the six statuses
Assert join_url non-null for the three active ones
Assert join_url null for the three terminal ones

description: A successful login stores the access token in sessionStorage and never in localStorage.
steps: Log in through the UI
Read sessionStorage and assert the token key exists
Read localStorage and assert it holds no token

description: After login a patient lands on the doctor search route, a doctor on the daily queue route and an admin on the user list route.
steps: Log in as each role
Assert the URL is /doctors for patient, /queue for doctor and /admin/users for admin

description: An unauthenticated visit to a protected route redirects to /login, a wrong-role visit shows the not-allowed page, and an unknown or another user's object shows the not-found page.
steps: Visit /queue unauthenticated and assert /login
Visit /admin/users as patient and assert the not-allowed page
Visit an appointment URL for another user's object and assert the not-found page

description: A 401 from any API call clears the session and redirects to /login, and a 503 shows a generic try-again message.
steps: Mock a 401 response and assert sessionStorage is cleared and URL is /login
Mock a 503 response and assert the text 'try again' is shown with no technical detail

description: Register and login screens show a duplicate-email message on 409 and one generic message on login failure, and have no horizontal scroll at 375px and 1280px.
steps: Submit register with a duplicate email and assert the inline message
Submit wrong login credentials and assert the single generic message
At 375px and at 1280px assert document scrollWidth <= clientWidth

description: Error messages are rendered in an ARIA live region, and every screen exposes loading, empty and error states.
steps: Trigger a login error and assert the message container has aria-live
Render a list screen with loading, empty and error mock states and assert each is displayed

description: The search page offers specialty, language, date-range filters and a sort control, lists results with the fee such as "500.00", and shows an empty state when nothing matches.
steps: Open the search page as a patient
Apply a specialty filter and assert results update
Assert each result card shows its fee
Apply filters matching nothing and assert the empty state

description: The doctor detail page shows open slots for the next 14 days grouped by date with times in browser-local zone and abbreviation such as '10:30 IST'.
steps: Open a doctor detail page with browser timezone Asia/Kolkata
Assert slots are grouped by date
Assert a slot label matches '\d{2}:\d{2} IST'

description: Selecting a slot and confirming shows a booking confirmation with doctor, local time and fee.
steps: Select a slot and press Confirm
Assert navigation to the confirmation view
Assert doctor name, local time and fee are shown

description: A 409 on booking shows an inline message and refreshes the slot list so the taken slot disappears.
steps: Mock POST /api/appointments returning 409 and a refreshed slot list without the slot
Confirm booking
Assert the inline message
Assert the slot is no longer listed

description: At 375px the patient screens have no horizontal scroll and every interactive control is at least 44px by 44px.
steps: Set viewport 375x800
On search and detail pages assert scrollWidth <= clientWidth
Measure all buttons and links and assert each bounding box >= 44px in both dimensions

description: My appointments lists each appointment with a status text label, and shows a 'Join video visit' control only for BOOKED, CHECKED_IN and IN_PROGRESS.
steps: Render appointments in all six statuses
Assert each card displays the status as text
Assert 'Join video visit' exists on the three active cards and not on the three terminal cards

description: Inside the last 60 minutes before start, Cancel and Reschedule are disabled with a visible explanation; outside it they are enabled.
steps: Render an appointment starting in 59 minutes
Assert Cancel and Reschedule are disabled and an explanation is visible
Render one starting in 61 minutes and assert both enabled

description: Confirming cancel updates the card to CANCELLED, and a 409 response shows an inline message instead.
steps: Click Cancel and Confirm with the API mocked to 200 and assert the card shows CANCELLED
Mock 409 and assert the inline message and unchanged status

description: Reschedule lets the patient pick another open slot of the same doctor and the card then shows the new time.
steps: Click Reschedule
Pick a different slot
Confirm
Assert the card time equals the new slot time

description: The consultation notes view for a completed appointment lists notes read-only with no edit or delete controls.
steps: Open a completed appointment with two notes
Assert both note texts are shown
Assert no edit, delete or input controls are present

description: The profile form saves changes, shows a success message, and re-loading the page shows the saved values.
steps: Edit the phone field and submit
Assert a success message
Reload the page and assert the new value is displayed
